content:
Typing < in the loogle searchbar sometimes clears all the text after the cursor position
Loogle! - Google Chrome 2026-03-10 18-03-06.mp4

Wait we don't sanitize the input? Try this: https://loogle.lean-lang.org/?q=%3Ch1+style%3D%22color%3A+red%22%3ETest%3Cbr%3E%3Cbutton+onclick%3D%22alert(%27hi%27);%22%3EClick%20me!%3C/button%3E%3C/h1%3E
wow, it's much worse than I thought
FWIW the < issue also happens in the VSCode extension's Loogle panel
The lean4 extension's panel? That's just a webview for the browser version more or less, so it probably carries over from the website
The fix is of course to escape inputs in the webpage and API

Shreyas Srinivas said:

The lean4 extension's panel? That's just a webview for the browser version more or less

No it isn't - the extension's Loogle is separate from Loogle's website.
But they do both use the same input component (@leanprover/unicode-input-component), which is likely why they share the same bug.
https://github.com/leanprover/vscode-lean4/blob/a884fa075489c3401e3702ad78aaa45a98a0841a/vscode-lean4/loogleview/index.ts#L172
That's a request to the backend, unrelated to frontend bugs
It was borrowed from the webpage version.
Of course the backend is shared, but the backend is not related to the current thread

Robin Arnez said:

Wait we don't sanitize the input? Try this: https://loogle.lean-lang.org/?q=%3Ch1+style%3D%22color%3A+red%22%3ETest%3Cbr%3E%3Cbutton+onclick%3D%22alert(%27hi%27);%22%3EClick%20me!%3C/button%3E%3C/h1%3E

classical xss, @Joachim Breitner !

https://loogle.lean-lang.org/?q=%3Cimg%20src=x%20onerror=alert(%27XSS%27)%3E
No, I mean the front end of this version was borrowed from that of the webpage

Jon Eugster said:

classical xss

:(
https://github.com/leanprover/vscode-lean4/blob/a884fa075489c3401e3702ad78aaa45a98a0841a/lean4-unicode-input-component/src/index.ts#L271C13-L273
The unicode input library is not the issue.
The issue is not sanitising the form input
This extension came 6-8 months after my loogle extension.
Fixing this isn't as simple as swapping innerHTML with textContent/value, because the UI uses it to render the underlines under abbreviations

I think the solution is overlaying a zero-height div with a border, positioned right where the in-progress abbreviation is being typed. It's also a good excuse to make the input monospace, to help calculating the offset

Shreyas Srinivas said:

The unicode input library is not the issue.

I think snir broshi's analysis is quite accurate. The input is sanitised initially (talking about the website here) using html.escape() but the the linked line of code sets the innerHtml which is where you'd need to take some action.

Good morning and thanks a lot for flagging this. This is somewhat embarrasing. I have removed the unicode input (should be deployed in a few minutes), until the unicode component has this fixed. Sorry for the temporary inconvenience.

Thanks a lot for reporting this (quite embarrassing) issue.

vscode-lean4#735 resolves the XSS issue. It has been published as 0.2.0 of the unicode input component.
If you are using the unicode input component, please update to 0.2.0.
Loogle should now work again as ususal

(The underlying issue here was that when I wrote this component for the LoogleView in the VS Code extension, I didn't give this issue too much thought because you can't link to the LoogleView, and then when I made it available for projects other than the LoogleView where this can be a problem, I failed to do another proper review that would have caught this. Sorry.)

Marc Huisinga said:

Thanks a lot for reporting this (quite embarrassing) issue.

vscode-lean4#735 resolves the XSS issue. It has been published as 0.2.0 of the unicode input component.
If you are using the unicode input component, please update to 0.2.0.

Can you put this in #announce ?
Do we have evidence of people using the unicode input component that would be reached by that and who are not following general? Seems out of proportion to put this on #announce
Jon's lean4monaco depends on it (though I couldn't find why), so perhaps #Editors & UIs since some people there develop Lean web GUIs?

thanks for the reminder. That was dead weight which could simply be dropped:

https://www.npmjs.com/package/lean4monaco?activeTab=dependencies

(it's imported in some files which are included through the hacky inclusion of vscode-lean4 in the project (e.g. "loogle-view"), but none of them are actually used anywhere so I think would be dropped by the bundler.)
(We published a low severity CVE for this, so it should show up in npm audit for packages that depend on the unicode input component)
